title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the real streets and corridors where Boston University students live, eat, and study beyond the official campus boundaries.

cards.title: The Heart of Allston Village
cards.subtitle: Harvard Avenue, Allston
cards.notes: Walk this corridor to find the city's highest concentration of student-friendly international eateries and thrift stores.
cards.short_summary: A major commercial spine in Allston known for diverse dining and high undergraduate residency.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Avenue is described as the spine of the Harvard Avenue Historic District and a major commercial and residential hub for students.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Allston | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public city street; most businesses open late until 10 PM or midnight.

cards.title: Allston's Main Dining Strip
cards.subtitle: Brighton Avenue, Allston
cards.notes: Visit this block for a dense row of ramen shops, taquerias, and Korean BBQ spots popular for off-campus group dinners.
cards.short_summary: A vibrant thoroughfare in Allston featuring a wide variety of global cuisines and student housing.
cards.evidence_claim: Brighton Avenue is noted for its high concentration of restaurants including ramen, Italian, and vegetarian options.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Allston | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; high pedestrian activity throughout the day and evening.

cards.title: The Brookline Connection
cards.subtitle: Beacon Street, Brookline
cards.notes: Ride the Green Line C branch along this street to access quieter residential blocks and local coffee shops.
cards.short_summary: A major Brookline thoroughfare that serves as a primary residential area for BU upperclassmen.
cards.evidence_claim: Beacon Street in Brookline is highlighted as a popular area for BU students seeking off-campus housing and transit access.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Coolidge Corner | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public street; primary route for the MBTA Green Line C branch.

cards.title: Gateway to the Fenway
cards.subtitle: Brookline Avenue, Fenway
cards.notes: Follow this road from Kenmore Square to reach the movie theater and major retail hubs in the Fenway district.
cards.short_summary: A key connector between Kenmore Square and the Fenway neighborhood's commercial center.
cards.evidence_claim: Brookline Avenue is part of the 'confusing convergence' at Kenmore Square and leads to the Fenway-Kenmore neighborhood.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Fenway-Kenmore | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public street; connects Kenmore Square to the Longwood Medical Area.

cards.title: Beside the Green Monster
cards.subtitle: Lansdowne Street, Fenway
cards.notes: Walk behind Fenway Park's famous wall to experience the game-day energy and visit major concert venues.
cards.short_summary: A famous street bordering Fenway Park known for its entertainment venues and proximity to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Lansdowne Street is described as having a 'crackle of excitement' and is home to House of Blues and other venues.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Fenway-Kenmore | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public street; often closed to vehicles during Red Sox home games.

cards.title: Fenway's Modern Corridor
cards.subtitle: Boylston Street, Fenway
cards.notes: Explore this block for the Time Out Market food hall and modern study-friendly cafes near the Fens.
cards.short_summary: A redeveloped stretch of Boylston Street featuring upscale dining, retail, and park access.
cards.evidence_claim: Trendy restaurants line Boylston Street in the Fenway neighborhood, near the Time Out Market food hall.
cards.source_title: Fenway Park, Restaurants, Hotels, Nightlife - Boston Discovery Guide
cards.access_notes: Public street; food hall and retail hours typically extend to 10 PM.

cards.title: The Packard's Corner Hub
cards.subtitle: Commonwealth Avenue, Allston
cards.notes: Stock up on groceries at the large Star Market or Super 88 at this busy intersection where campus meets Allston.
cards.short_summary: The western extension of the main campus artery, serving as a major retail anchor for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Packard's Corner is the intersection of Harvard Street, Brighton Avenue, and Commonwealth Avenue, catering to students.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Allston | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public street; Star Market is open 24 hours or late night depending on current policy.

cards.title: Historic Brownstone Row
cards.subtitle: Bay State Road, Boston
cards.notes: Walk this leafy, quiet street to see the historic brownstones that house many of BU's specialty residential communities.
cards.short_summary: A picturesque residential street in BU's East Campus known for its historic architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: Bay State Road is described as one of Boston's most picturesque streets, featuring charming brownstones.
cards.source_title: Bay State Road Brownstones - Housing - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; very quiet compared to the parallel Commonwealth Avenue.

cards.title: The Iconic Citgo Gateway
cards.subtitle: Kenmore Square, Boston
cards.notes: Meet friends under the Citgo sign at this major transit hub that connects the East Campus to the rest of Boston.
cards.short_summary: A famous commercial square and transit hub at the eastern edge of the BU campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenmore Square is the 'culinary heart' of campus life and a major convergence of streets and transit.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Fenway-Kenmore | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public square; major MBTA station for Green Line B, C, and D branches.

cards.title: The South Campus Link
cards.subtitle: St. Mary's Street, Brookline
cards.notes: Cross the bridge on this street to move between the main campus and the 'South Campus' residential area in Brookline.
cards.short_summary: A street connecting BU's central campus to its South Campus housing and the town of Brookline.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Mary's Street is a primary route for students walking from Commonwealth Avenue to the South Campus area.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Coolidge Corner | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public street; includes a bridge over the MBTA tracks and the Mass Pike.
